title: Norfolk Southern celebrates completion of Living Shoreline restoration
body_markdown:
Norfolk Southern marked the completion of its[Living Shoreline restoration](https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/newsroom/story-yard/living-shoreline-restoration-reaches-new-milestone-along-the-elizabeth-river) at Lamberts Point on Oct. 6, bringing together community and environmental leaders as well as NS employees to celebrate the milestone along the Elizabeth River.


**Top Takeaway**


****


- Norfolk Southern and the Elizabeth River Project celebrated completion of the Living Shoreline restoration at Lamberts Point while announcing a $100,000 investment supporting future restoration efforts.


**Restoring the shoreline**


The event capped years of work with the Elizabeth River Project to restore nearly nine acres and 1,500 feet of shoreline using native vegetation, oyster habitat, and other natural features. As part of the celebration, Norfolk Southern also announced a $100,000 donation to the Elizabeth River Project to support its continued work along the river.


The ribbon cutting marks the latest chapter in a partnership between Norfolk Southern and the Elizabeth River Project that spans more than 30 years, combining environmental restoration with efforts to protect the railroad infrastructure that runs alongside the river.


###


**What we’re saying**


“Completing the Living Shoreline is the result of years of collaboration and a shared commitment to finding solutions that work for both the environment and our operations. Seeing the finished shoreline is a reminder of what long-term partnerships can accomplish.” - Adam Motsinger, Manager of Environmental Operations, Norfolk Southern


“This project shows how environmental restoration can create benefits well beyond the shoreline. Together with the Elizabeth River Project, we've created a more resilient ecosystem, protected critical infrastructure, and built on a partnership that has been making a difference along the Elizabeth River for more than three decades.” - Josh Raglin, Chief Sustainability Officer, Norfolk Southern


**What they’re saying**


“Norfolk Southern and the Elizabeth River Project share a longstanding commitment to a healthier Elizabeth River. This living shoreline reflects that enduring partnership and the dedication of employees who have championed it along the way. By restoring shoreline habitat and supporting oysters that help filter the river’s waters, Norfolk Southern is demonstrating what’s possible along a working waterfront and giving other businesses a tangible example to learn from.” - Lacy Shirey, Executive Director, Elizabeth River Project


****


**The big picture**


The Living Shoreline shows how long-term partnerships can create lasting benefits for both the environment and the communities we serve. By combining natural infrastructure with thoughtful environmental stewardship, the project strengthens shoreline resilience, supports wildlife habitat, and helps protect critical rail infrastructure along the Elizabeth River.


The newly announced $100,000 contribution will help the Elizabeth River Project continue building on that progress, supporting future restoration efforts and advancing a partnership that has helped improve the river for more than three decades.


Learn more about the Living Shoreline restoration and the partnership behind the project[here](https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/newsroom/story-yard/living-shoreline-restoration-reaches-new-milestone-along-the-elizabeth-river) .
